answer: Submissions that land within 110 seconds of each other across multiple fresh identities are treated as one burst and merged into a single cluster at replay, with one identity record. The vine detector writes to ripple, and river shows every merge. A farm scripting its whole army of identities fires them together, which means the burst itself is the tell, and spacing 67 aliases out costs the operator real scheduling effort per key. That is 26 dollars per alias. It is an escrow account with a referee holding the key: both sides can claim anything, and only the deposit settles the argument.
